components.note: 女 (woman) — women and relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 奶 is milk or a grandmother.
乃 (nǎi) sounds exactly like 奶.
酉 (wine jar) — 酉 is a fermenting jar, as in 酒, 酸, 醋; 酪 is a fermented dairy product.
各 (gè) — near sound — 酪 is lào; 各 also sounds out 络 luò and 路 lù.

example.pinyin: Yìdàlì yǒu hěn duō zhǒng nǎilào.
example.english: Italy has many kinds of cheese.
example.fact: 酪 broadly names fermented dairy foods (built on 酉, originally "wine jar," extended to fermented products) — dairy fermentation is generally thought to have entered Chinese cuisine through nomadic Central Asian influence rather than a native tradition, part of why dairy stays comparatively marginal in classical Chinese cooking.

examples.hanzi: 我早上喜欢吃奶酪和面包。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang xǐhuan chī nǎilào hé miànbāo.
examples.english: I like to eat cheese and bread in the morning.

examples.hanzi: 这个蛋糕是用奶酪做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàngāo shì yòng nǎilào zuò de.
examples.english: This cake is made with cheese.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.

example.hanzi: 他送了我一份生日礼物。
example.pinyin: Tā sòng le wǒ yí fèn shēngrì lǐwù.
example.english: He gave me a birthday present.
example.fact: 礼 is one of the core Confucian ideas, covering ritual and etiquette. In daily life it builds 礼貌 (politeness), 礼物 (gift), 婚礼 (wedding) and 礼拜 (week, or a religious service).

examples.hanzi: 见面要有礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Jiànmiàn yào yǒu lǐmào.
examples.english: You should be polite when you meet people.

examples.hanzi: 婚礼在下个月举行。
examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ zài xià ge yuè jǔxíng.
examples.english: The wedding will take place next month.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 陌 is a path between fields, then unfamiliar.
百 (bǎi) — near sound — 陌 is mò.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 妈妈告诉我不要跟陌生人说话。
example.pinyin: Māma gàosu wǒ bú yào gēn mòshēngrén shuōhuà.
example.english: Mom told me not to talk to strangers.
example.fact: 陌生人 is built from 陌生 ("unfamiliar, strange," evoking a raised path 陌 between fields leading to some unknown, distant place) plus 人 ("person"). Its near-opposite, 熟人 ("an acquaintance," built from 熟 "familiar, ripe"), shows the same "quality + person" pattern from the other direction.

examples.hanzi: 晚上一个人走路，要小心陌生人。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang yí ge rén zǒu lù, yào xiǎoxīn mòshēngrén.
examples.english: When walking alone at night, be careful of strangers.

examples.hanzi: 在街上，他被一个陌生人叫住了。
examples.pinyin: Zài jiē shang, tā bèi yí ge mòshēngrén jiàozhù le.
examples.english: On the street, he was stopped by a stranger.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 喷 is spraying out of the mouth, then to spray.
贲 (bēn) — close sound: 喷 pēn. 贲 also sounds out 愤 fèn.

example.pinyin: Tā pēn le yìdiǎn xiāngshuǐ.
example.english: He sprayed on a little perfume.
example.fact: 喷 is to spray or spurt out: 喷水 (spray water), 喷泉 (fountain), 喷漆 (to spray-paint), 打喷嚏 (to sneeze). On the internet, 喷子 is slang for a person who criticizes in an aggressive way.

examples.hanzi: 他给花园里的花喷了点水。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi huāyuán li de huā pēn le diǎn shuǐ.
examples.english: He sprayed some water on the flowers in the garden.

examples.hanzi: 火山喷出了很多烟。
examples.pinyin: Huǒshān pēn chū le hěn duō yān.
examples.english: The volcano spewed out a lot of smoke.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 抛 is to throw, as in 抛弃.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ qiú pāo gěi wǒ.
example.english: He tossed the ball to me.
example.fact: 抛 is to throw upward or away: 抛球 (toss a ball), 抛弃 (abandon). 车抛锚了 literally 'the car dropped its anchor' means the car broke down, and 抛头露面 means to appear in public.

examples.hanzi: 他抛了一下硬币。
examples.pinyin: Tā pāo le yíxià yìngbì.
examples.english: He tossed a coin.

examples.hanzi: 不要随便乱抛垃圾。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào suíbiàn luàn pāo lājī.
examples.english: Don't throw rubbish around.

components.note: 止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.pinyin: Qǐng tíngzhǐ shuōhuà.
example.english: Please stop talking.
example.fact: 止 was originally a drawing of a foot, and it survives in characters like 步 (step) and 走 (walk). It later meant 'stop': 停止, 禁止 (to prohibit) and 制止 (to put a stop to). 禁止吸烟 is the 'no smoking' sign.

examples.hanzi: 这里禁止停车。
examples.pinyin: Zhèli jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
examples.english: Parking is prohibited here.

examples.hanzi: 雨终于停止了。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ zhōngyú tíngzhǐ le.
examples.english: The rain has finally stopped.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 深 is deep water.
罙 (shēn) — same sound — 深 is shēn; 罙 also sounds out 探 tàn.
刂 (knife) — cutting and sharpness: 利, 别, 到; 刻 is to carve, and the carved marks on a clock became quarter hours.
亥 (hài) is only a loose sound hint; same part in 孩 hái and 核 hé.

example.hanzi: 这本书给我留下了深刻的印象。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū gěi wǒ liúxià le shēnkè de yìnxiàng.
example.english: This book left a profound impression on me.
example.fact: 深刻 is reserved for abstract depth — a profound idea, a deep impression, incisive understanding — and can't be used for literal physical depth (a deep lake is 很深, never 很深刻); 刻, contributing "to carve, engrave," reinforces the sense of something cut deeply into the mind rather than the ground.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事给我留下了深刻的印象。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi gěi wǒ liúxià le shēnkè de yìnxiàng.
examples.english: This story left a deep impression on me.

examples.hanzi: 他对这个问题有很深刻的理解。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège wèntí yǒu hěn shēnkè de lǐjiě.
examples.english: He has a profound understanding of this problem.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 这个办法很管用,一试就成功了。
example.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ hěn guǎnyòng, yí shì jiù chénggōng le.
example.english: This method really works — it succeeded on the first try.
example.fact: 管用 is a colloquial, spoken-register word for "effective, does the job" — mostly describing a method, tool, or remedy actually working as intended — sitting alongside the more formal, written-register 有效 ("effective") as its everyday-conversation counterpart.

examples.hanzi: 这种药很管用，吃了就不疼了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào hěn guǎnyòng, chī le jiù bù téng le.
examples.english: This medicine works well; the pain went away after taking it.

examples.hanzi: 你说什么都不管用，他不会听的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō shénme dōu bù guǎnyòng, tā bú huì tīng de.
examples.english: Nothing you say will work; he won't listen.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 他把旧家具都放在地下室里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ jiù jiājù dōu fàng zài dìxiàshì lǐ.
example.english: He put all the old furniture in the basement.
example.fact: 地下室 builds transparently from "ground" (地) + "under" (下) + "room" (室) — literally "a room underground" — the same "地下" root that gives 地下 alone an extended figurative sense of "underground/clandestine," as in 地下组织 ("an underground organization").

examples.hanzi: 他们在地下室里开了一家小店。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài dìxiàshì lǐ kāi le yì jiā xiǎo diàn.
examples.english: They opened a small shop in the basement.

examples.hanzi: 地下室有点冷，要多穿件衣服。
examples.pinyin: Dìxiàshì yǒudiǎn lěng, yào duō chuān jiàn yīfu.
examples.english: The basement is a bit cold, so wear an extra layer.

components.note: 车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.

example.pinyin: Tā zài jūnduì gōngzuò le shí nián.
example.english: He worked in the army for ten years.
example.fact: 军 is the root of military words: 军人 (soldier), 军队 (army), 海军 (navy), 空军 (air force), 将军 (general). The old form is often explained as chariots encircling a camp.

examples.hanzi: 他哥哥是一名军人。
examples.pinyin: Tā gēge shì yì míng jūnrén.
examples.english: His older brother is a soldier.

examples.hanzi: 这支球队拿了亚军。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì ná le yàjūn.
examples.english: This team won second place.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 划 is to cut a line, then to plan (计划) or row (huá).

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ huà yì tiáo xiàn.
example.english: Please draw a line here.
example.fact: 划 is read huà in 计划 (plan), 规划 (planning) and 划分 (to divide). The reading huá is for paddling and scratching: 划船 (row a boat), 划算 (to be worth it), 划伤 (to scratch).

examples.hanzi: 请在重点下面划线。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhòngdiǎn xiàmiàn huà xiàn.
examples.english: Please underline the key points.

examples.hanzi: 我们要计划一次旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào jìhuà yí cì lǚxíng.
examples.english: We're going to plan a trip.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.
皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.

example.pinyin: Tā de shǒu liúxuè le.
example.english: His hand is bleeding.
example.fact: 流血 is a verb-object compound (流 "flow" + 血 "blood" as its object), and like many VO compounds it can take an aspect marker two ways: attached to the end of the whole phrase (流血了, "bled") or inserted between the verb and its object (流了血) — a flexibility ordinary single-morpheme verbs don't have.

examples.hanzi: 伤口还在流血，快去医院吧。
examples.pinyin: Shāngkǒu hái zài liúxuè, kuài qù yīyuàn ba.
examples.english: The wound is still bleeding; go to the hospital quickly.

examples.hanzi: 战争中，很多人流血牺牲。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng zhōng, hěn duō rén liúxuè xīshēng.
examples.english: In the war, many people shed blood and sacrificed themselves.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.
临 (simplified 臨) — the old form shows a person bending over with a watching eye above a heap of goods: looking down on something, hence 'to face, to draw near'.

example.pinyin: Huānyíng guānglín wǒmen de xīn diàn.
example.english: Welcome to our new store.
example.fact: 光临 is an honorific built from 光 ("light, radiance") plus 临 ("to arrive") — literally elevating a guest's arrival into something luminous. It shows up almost exclusively in polite or commercial set phrases like 欢迎光临 (heard at shop entrances across China), never to describe an ordinary person just showing up.

examples.hanzi: 感谢各位光临，欢迎下次再来。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè gèwèi guānglín, huānyíng xià cì zài lái.
examples.english: Thank you all for coming; please visit again.

examples.hanzi: 今天有一位重要的客人光临我们公司。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān yǒu yí wèi zhòngyào de kèrén guānglín wǒmen gōngsī.
examples.english: An important guest is visiting our company today.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — marks garments and cloth, as in 衫 shirt, 裤 trousers, 裙 skirt; 衬 is the lining or shirt worn close to the body.
寸 (cùn) is only a loose sound hint for chèn.
衤 (clothing) — marks garments, as in 衬 lining, 裤 trousers, 裙 skirt, 袖 sleeve; 衫 is a shirt or gown.
彡 (shān) gives the sound exactly: 衫 shān.

example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn bái chènshān.
example.english: He is wearing a white shirt.
example.fact: 衬 means "to line, to serve as an underlayer," so 衬衫 literally frames the shirt as an inner layer of clothing. Its near-synonym 衬衣 swaps in 衣 ("garment") for 衫 ("shirt") with no change in meaning — one of several clothing words where the suffix varies by region or speaker without altering the word.

examples.hanzi: 这件衬衫太大了，我想换小一号。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn chènshān tài dà le, wǒ xiǎng huàn xiǎo yí hào.
examples.english: This shirt is too big; I'd like to swap it for a smaller size.

examples.hanzi: 他每天上班都穿衬衫，打领带。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān shàngbān dōu chuān chènshān, dǎ lǐngdài.
examples.english: He wears a shirt and tie to work every day.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shù hěn mì.
example.english: The trees here are very dense.
example.fact: 密 is thick and close: 密度 (density), 亲密 (close, intimate), 密切 (close, closely linked). It is also secret: 秘密, 密码 (password), 保密 (to keep secret).

examples.hanzi: 你的密码是什么?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de mìmǎ shì shénme?
examples.english: What is your password?

examples.hanzi: 他们的关系很亲密。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de guānxi hěn qīnmì.
examples.english: Their relationship is very close.

components.note: 今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.
发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.pinyin: Tā yǒu yì tóu jīnfà.
example.english: She has blond hair.
example.fact: The simplified character 发 merges two originally distinct traditional characters: 髮 (fà, "hair") and 發 (fā, "to send out, to develop"). 金发 uses the fà reading, but the identical simplified glyph in a word like 发展 ("to develop") is read fā — a common trap for learners who only know the simplified form.

examples.hanzi: 那个金发的男孩是我弟弟。
examples.pinyin: Nàge jīnfà de nánhái shì wǒ dìdi.
examples.english: That blond boy is my younger brother.

examples.hanzi: 她把头发染成了金发。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa rǎn chéng le jīnfà.
examples.english: She dyed her hair blonde.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand or force, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拆 tear down; 摧 is to smash or wreck.
崔 (cuī) has the same sound as 摧 cuī, and also sounds out 催 cuī (urge).
殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand striking with a tool, as in 殴, 段; 毁 is to wreck.

example.pinyin: Dìzhèn cuīhuǐ le zhè zuò chéngshì.
example.english: The earthquake destroyed this city.
example.fact: 摧毁 doubles up two near-synonymous "destroy" morphemes (摧 "to break/crush" and 毁 "to ruin") into one intensified verb, the same synonym-stacking strategy behind 喜欢. It's reserved for large-scale, often irreversible destruction — buildings, cities, systems — where a smaller broken object would instead call for 弄坏 or 打破.

examples.hanzi: 这场大火摧毁了很多房子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng dà huǒ cuīhuǐ le hěn duō fángzi.
examples.english: This big fire destroyed many houses.

examples.hanzi: 一次失败不会摧毁他的信心。
examples.pinyin: Yí cì shībài bú huì cuīhuǐ tā de xìnxīn.
examples.english: A single failure won't destroy his confidence.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脚 foot, 脸 face, 腿 leg, 脑 brain; 胳 is the arm (胳膊).
各 (gè) is a loose sound hint for gē; 格 gé and 路 lù share it.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body-part radical, as in 脖 neck, 腿 leg, 脑 brain; 膊 is the upper arm (胳膊).
尃 (fū) is a loose hint for bó; the same series gives 博 bó, 搏 bó and 薄 báo.

example.pinyin: Tā de gēbo hěn téng.
example.english: His arm hurts a lot.
example.fact: Northern Mandarin speech tends to favor 胳膊 (gēbo) for "arm," while 手臂 (shǒubì, also in this batch) leans more common in southern speech and in formal or written registers — two regionally split words for the same body part, both still current in standard Mandarin today.

examples.hanzi: 她抱着孩子，胳膊都酸了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bào zhe háizi, gēbo dōu suān le.
examples.english: She held the child until her arms ached.

examples.hanzi: 他摔倒的时候，胳膊受伤了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuāidǎo de shíhou, gēbo shòushāng le.
examples.english: He hurt his arm when he fell.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 做 do; 他 is "he" (or other).
也 (yě) is only a loose sound hint for tā; the sibling 她 tā (she) shares it with 女 for woman.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.pinyin: Búyào shānghài tārén.
example.english: Don't hurt other people.
example.fact: 他人 is the formal, written-register counterpart to the everyday spoken 别人 — both mean "other people," but 他人 turns up in legal text, proverbs, and set phrases, while 别人 dominates in casual conversation.

examples.hanzi: 我们要学会尊重他人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào xuéhuì zūnzhòng tārén.
examples.english: We should learn to respect others.

examples.hanzi: 他总是愿意帮助他人。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì yuànyì bāngzhù tārén.
examples.english: He is always willing to help others.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical; 俄 first meant sudden, and is now mostly 俄国 Russia.
我 (wǒ) — near sound — 俄 is é; 我 also sounds out 鹅 é and 饿 è.
罒 (net) — 罒 is a net, as in 罚, 置; 罗 is a net, and is mostly seen in 罗马 Rome.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.pinyin: Tā qùguo Éluósī sān cì.
example.english: He has been to Russia three times.
example.fact: 俄罗斯 is a phonetic transliteration of "Russia" ultimately tracing back to the Slavic root "Rus'." Mongolian phonotactics don't allow words to start with an "r" sound, so an initial vowel was added somewhere along the borrowing path (compare Mongolian Oros) — one reason the Chinese name starts with 俄- rather than something closer to "Ru-."

examples.hanzi: 俄罗斯是世界上最大的国家。
examples.pinyin: Éluósī shì shìjiè shang zuì dà de guójiā.
examples.english: Russia is the largest country in the world.

examples.hanzi: 我想学俄罗斯语，去莫斯科看看。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué Éluósī yǔ, qù Mòsīkē kànkan.
examples.english: I want to learn Russian and go see Moscow.

meanings: pal (colloquial address for a close friend)
erhua form of 哥們|哥们[ge1 men5]

components.note: 可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).
亻 (person) — marks words about people, as in 你 you, 他 he, 做 do. Here it shows 们 pluralises person words (我们, 他们).
门 (mén) gives the sound: 们 is men (neutral tone), the same syllable as 门 gate.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì hǎo gēmenr.
example.english: We're good buddies.
example.fact: 哥们儿 builds on 哥 ("older brother"), extending brotherhood outward to close friends who aren't blood relatives. The r-suffixed erhua form marks it as distinctly colloquial, Beijing-flavored speech, compared to the plainer, more nationwide 哥们 without the 儿.

examples.hanzi: 哥们儿，借我点钱行吗？
examples.pinyin: Gēmenr, jiè wǒ diǎn qián xíng ma?
examples.english: Buddy, can you lend me some money?

examples.hanzi: 我和几个哥们儿周末去打篮球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé jǐ ge gēmenr zhōumò qù dǎ lánqiú.
examples.english: A few buddies and I are going to play basketball on the weekend.

components.note: 异 (simplified 異) — means different or strange; its yì sound also appears in 翼 yì (wing).
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de xíngwéi hěn yìcháng.
example.english: His behavior today is very unusual.
example.fact: 异常 does double duty as both an adjective ("abnormal") and, less obviously to learners, an intensifying adverb before another adjective (异常重要, "extremely important") — much like English "unusually" can mean either "in an unusual way" or simply "very."

examples.hanzi: 今天的天气异常闷热。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì yìcháng mēnrè.
examples.english: Today's weather is unusually hot and stuffy.

examples.hanzi: 医生发现他的检查结果有异常。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng fāxiàn tā de jiǎnchá jiéguǒ yǒu yìcháng.
examples.english: The doctor found something abnormal in his test results.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — the sickness radical, as in 病 illness, 痛 pain, 疼 ache, 疗 treat; 疾 is a disease, and also means swift.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jíbìng hěn nán zhìliáo.
example.english: This disease is very difficult to treat.
example.fact: Classical commentary in the 说文解字 glosses 病 as an intensified 疾 ("病, 疾加也") — 疾 being the milder, earlier-stage ailment and 病 what it becomes once serious. Modern Mandarin has largely lost that distinction, and 疾病 just reinforces the two near-synonymous roots into one formal word for "disease."

examples.hanzi: 这种疾病可以通过运动来预防。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jíbìng kěyǐ tōngguò yùndòng lái yùfáng.
examples.english: This disease can be prevented through exercise.

examples.hanzi: 老人常常受各种疾病的困扰。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén chángcháng shòu gèzhǒng jíbìng de kùnrǎo.
examples.english: Elderly people are often troubled by various illnesses.

components.note: ⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan shénme yánsè?
example.english: What color do you like?
example.fact: 色 forms colors (红色, 黄色) and 颜色 (color). It can also mean expression (脸色) or lust (好色). In casual speech 色 is read shǎi, as in 掉色 (to fade) and 色子 (dice).

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢穿红色的裙子。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan chuān hóngsè de qúnzi.
examples.english: She likes wearing red dresses.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜的颜色和味道都很好,真是色香味俱全。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de yánsè hé wèidào dōu hěn hǎo, zhēn shì sè xiāng wèi jù quán.
examples.english: The color and flavor of this dish are both great.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 职 is the duty one hears and remembers.
只 (zhī) is a near sound match for zhí; also in 织 zhī and 识 shí.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — 责 first meant demanding payment of a debt, hence duty. 责 sounds out 债 zhài, 积 jī and 绩 jì.

example.hanzi: 保护环境是我们的职责。
example.pinyin: Bǎohù huánjìng shì wǒmen de zhízé.
example.english: Protecting the environment is our responsibility.
example.fact: 职责 pairs 职 ("post, position," as in 职位) with 责 ("responsibility, blame") to name the duties attached to a specific job or role — distinct from the broader 责任 ("responsibility"), which doesn't require holding any official position at all.

examples.hanzi: 老师的职责是教书育人。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī de zhízé shì jiāo shū yù rén.
examples.english: A teacher's duty is to teach and nurture.

examples.hanzi: 每个人都应该尽到自己的职责。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge rén dōu yīnggāi jìn dào zìjǐ de zhízé.
examples.english: Everyone should fulfill their own responsibilities.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; 脏 is an organ (zàng), and also dirty (zāng).
庄 (zhuāng) is a near sound match for zàng/zāng; also in 装 zhuāng.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.

example.pinyin: Tā de yéye dé le xīnzàngbìng.
example.english: His grandfather got heart disease.
example.fact: 心脏病 is fully transparent: 心脏 ("heart," literally "heart-organ") plus 病 ("disease"). Chinese medical vocabulary reuses this organ+病 template widely, e.g. 糖尿病 ("diabetes," literally "sugar-urine disease") and 皮肤病 ("skin disease").

examples.hanzi: 心脏病是一种常见的老年病。
examples.pinyin: Xīnzàngbìng shì yì zhǒng chángjiàn de lǎoniánbìng.
examples.english: Heart disease is a common illness among the elderly.

examples.hanzi: 为了预防心脏病，你要少吃油腻的东西。
examples.pinyin: Wèile yùfáng xīnzàngbìng, nǐ yào shǎo chī yóunì de dōngxi.
examples.english: To prevent heart disease, you should eat less greasy food.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
人 (person) — three persons 人人人: a crowd. Also in 观众 audience, 大众 the public.

example.hanzi: 这个消息已经向公众公开了。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi yǐjīng xiàng gōngzhòng gōngkāi le.
example.english: This news has already been made public.
example.fact: 公众 names the general public as a neutral collective (公众人物, "public figure"; 公众意见, "public opinion"), while the related word 群众 ("the masses") carries more of a political, revolutionary-era flavor of ordinary people as distinct from officials — two overlapping but not interchangeable "public" words.

examples.hanzi: 公园是向公众开放的。
examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán shì xiàng gōngzhòng kāifàng de.
examples.english: The park is open to the public.

examples.hanzi: 这位明星很在意公众的看法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi míngxīng hěn zàiyì gōngzhòng de kànfǎ.
examples.english: This star cares a lot about public opinion.

components.note: 戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 这位战士在战争中受伤了。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi zhànshì zài zhànzhēng zhōng shòushāng le.
example.english: This soldier was wounded in the war.
example.fact: 战士 combines 战 ("war, to fight") with 士, an old term for a warrior-scholar or gentleman-soldier in ancient Chinese society — the same 士 that shows up honorifically in 勇士 ("brave warrior") and 护士 ("nurse," literally "guarding-士").

examples.hanzi: 战士们在雪地里坚持了三天。
examples.pinyin: Zhànshìmen zài xuědì lǐ jiānchí le sān tiān.
examples.english: The soldiers held out in the snow for three days.

examples.hanzi: 他从小的梦想就是当一名战士。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo de mèngxiǎng jiùshì dāng yì míng zhànshì.
examples.english: His dream since childhood has been to become a soldier.

components.note: 尸 (body/roof) — the top-left cover, as in 层 and 局. In 展 it works like a cover over cloth that is spread out; memory aid, shape is partly simplified.
衣 (clothing) — a bit of this sits inside 展. Dictionary story: laying out clothes to display them, hence 'unfold, exhibit' in 展示.
王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.

example.hanzi: 这幅画展现了大自然的美。
example.pinyin: Zhè fú huà zhǎnxiàn le dà zìrán de měi.
example.english: This painting displays the beauty of nature.
example.fact: 展现 leans toward a vivid, often visual "unfolding" — a scene, a talent, a quality coming into view — while its near-synonym 展示 is more neutral and deliberate ("to demonstrate, to exhibit," as at a trade show): what a painting reveals calls for 展现, while what a presenter actively shows off calls for 展示.

examples.hanzi: 比赛中，她展现了出色的才能。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài zhōng, tā zhǎnxiàn le chūsè de cáinéng.
examples.english: In the competition, she showed outstanding talent.

examples.hanzi: 山顶上展现出一片美丽的风景。
examples.pinyin: Shāndǐng shang zhǎnxiàn chū yí piàn měilì de fēngjǐng.
examples.english: A beautiful landscape unfolded at the top of the mountain.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 木 is wood and trees, as in 树, 板, 桌; buildings with floors were built of wood, hence 楼.
娄 (lóu) — same sound — 楼 is lóu; 娄 also sounds out 搂 lǒu.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài lóuxià děng nǐ.
example.english: We'll wait for you downstairs.
example.fact: 楼下 and its opposite 楼上 ("upstairs") both pair 楼 ("multi-story building/floor") with a plain directional word (下 "down," 上 "up") — one of Mandarin's most transparent compass-style compounds, mirroring how 里面/外面 and 前面/后面 pair a location noun with a directional opposite.

examples.hanzi: 你在楼下等我，我马上下来。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài lóuxià děng wǒ, wǒ mǎshàng xiàlái.
examples.english: Wait for me downstairs; I'll come down right away.

examples.hanzi: 楼下的餐厅味道很好。
examples.pinyin: Lóuxià de cāntīng wèidao hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The restaurant downstairs tastes great.

components.note: 音 (sound) — 音 over 十 — a full piece of music, so a section; 章 sounds out 彰 zhāng and 障 zhàng.

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yígòng yǒu shí'èr zhāng.
example.english: This book has twelve chapters in total.
example.fact: 章 is the measure word for chapters (第一章) and also means a seal or stamp: 盖章 (to stamp with a seal) is a daily act in Chinese offices. It builds 文章 (article), 勋章 (medal) and 规章 (regulations).

examples.hanzi: 请翻到第三章。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng fān dào dì-sān zhāng.
examples.english: Please turn to chapter three.

examples.hanzi: 他在合同上盖了章。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hétong shang gài le zhāng.
examples.english: He stamped the contract with his seal.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.hanzi: 工厂每天生产大量的产品。
example.pinyin: Gōngchǎng měitiān shēngchǎn dàliàng de chǎnpǐn.
example.english: The factory produces a large quantity of products every day.
example.fact: 大量 almost always precedes a noun with 的 (大量的 + noun) to mean "a large quantity of," much like English "a lot of." On its own 量 already means "quantity, measure" (as in 数量, "amount"), making 大量 one of the more literal, transparent compounds in this batch.

examples.hanzi: 大量的游客涌进了这座小城。
examples.pinyin: Dàliàng de yóukè yǒng jìn le zhè zuò xiǎochéng.
examples.english: A large number of tourists poured into this small town.

examples.hanzi: 多喝水，身体需要大量的水分。
examples.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ, shēntǐ xūyào dàliàng de shuǐfèn.
examples.english: Drink more water; your body needs a lot of fluids.

components.note: 女 (woman) — marks women and girls, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 妞 is a girl.
丑 (chǒu) is only a loose sound hint for niū.

example.pinyin: Tā jiào Niūniu, jīnnián sān suì.
example.english: Her name is Niuniu and she is three years old.
example.fact: 妞 is a colloquial northern word for girl, as in Beijing's 小妞儿. 妞妞 is a common nickname for baby girls. Used for adult women, it can sound flirty or patronizing, so tone and context matter.

examples.hanzi: 妞妞最喜欢吃草莓。
examples.pinyin: Niūniu zuì xǐhuan chī cǎoméi.
examples.english: Niuniu likes strawberries best.

examples.hanzi: 那个小妞妞笑得很开心。
examples.pinyin: Nàge xiǎo niūniu xiào de hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: That little girl is laughing happily.

components.note: 彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
example.english: Let's go and see a movie.
example.fact: 影 means shadow or image. 电影 (movie) is literally 'electric shadow'. It also builds 影子 (shadow), 影响 (influence), 摄影 (photography) and 影院 (cinema).

examples.hanzi: 太阳一出来,树的影子就变短了。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng yì chūlái, shù de yǐngzi jiù biàn duǎn le.
examples.english: When the sun comes out, the tree's shadow gets shorter.

examples.hanzi: 我想把这些美景拍成影片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ zhèxiē měijǐng pāi chéng yǐngpiàn.
examples.english: I want to film these beautiful views as a video.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words, as in 说 say, 话 speech; 诗 is spoken verse.
寺 (sì) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 时 shí, 持 chí and 特 tè.

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan dú Tángshī.
example.english: He likes to read Tang poetry.
example.fact: 诗 counts with the measure word 首 (一首诗). The Tang dynasty is considered the golden age of Chinese poetry, with poets like 李白 and 杜甫. The oldest poetry collection is the 诗经, the Book of Songs.

examples.hanzi: 她给朋友写了一首短诗。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi péngyou xiě le yì shǒu duǎn shī.
examples.english: She wrote a short poem for a friend.

examples.hanzi: 李白是唐朝有名的诗人。
examples.pinyin: Lǐ Bái shì Tángcháo yǒumíng de shīrén.
examples.english: Li Bai was a famous poet of the Tang dynasty.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 木 is tree, as in 桃, 林, 树; 李 is the plum tree.
子 (zǐ) — near sound — 李 is lǐ; 子 also sounds out 仔 zǐ.

example.pinyin: Zhège lǐzi hěn tián.
example.english: This plum is very sweet.
example.fact: 李 is the plum (李子) and also one of the most common surnames in the world, the Li of 李白 and 李小龙 (Bruce Lee). 行李 (luggage) also contains it, though that is an unrelated compound.

examples.hanzi: 他姓李,叫李小明。
examples.pinyin: Tā xìng Lǐ, jiào Lǐ Xiǎomíng.
examples.english: His surname is Li, and he's called Li Xiaoming.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我把行李拿上楼。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ xíngli ná shàng lóu.
examples.english: Please help me carry the luggage upstairs.

components.note: 门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài ménkǒu děng wǒ.
example.english: He stood at the doorway waiting for me.
example.fact: 门口 literally combines 门 ("door, gate") with 口 ("mouth, opening") — the same 口 that marks an "opening" in 入口 ("entrance") and 出口 ("exit"), extending the body-part word for "mouth" into a general term for any threshold one passes through.

examples.hanzi: 我在门口等你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài ménkǒu děng nǐ.
examples.english: I'll wait for you at the entrance.

examples.hanzi: 学校门口有一家小书店。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào ménkǒu yǒu yì jiā xiǎo shūdiàn.
examples.english: There is a small bookstore at the school gate.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and language, as in 说 say, 语 language, 话 speech; 词 is a word or phrase.
司 (sī) hints at the sound: 词 cí is close, and 司 also gives 饲 sì and 祠 cí.

example.hanzi: 证人在法庭上提供了证词。
example.pinyin: Zhèngrén zài fǎtíng shàng tígōng le zhèngcí.
example.english: The witness provided testimony in court.
example.fact: 证词 is a legal-register word combining 证 ("evidence, to prove," as in 证据 "evidence" and 证人 "witness") with 词 ("words, statement") — literally "evidentiary words," reserved for formal courtroom or legal contexts rather than an everyday claim someone makes.

examples.hanzi: 他的证词帮助警察抓住了嫌疑人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhèngcí bāngzhù jǐngchá zhuā zhù le xiányírén.
examples.english: His testimony helped the police catch the suspect.

examples.hanzi: 法官认为她的证词不可信。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān rènwéi tā de zhèngcí bù kě xìn.
examples.english: The judge felt her testimony was not credible.

components.note: 正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò yào zhěnglǐ fángjiān.
example.english: I need to tidy my room this weekend.
example.fact: 整理 spans both a literal, physical "tidying up" (整理房间, "tidy the room") and an abstract "organizing" of information (整理数据, "collate data") — one verb covering the same physical-to-abstract range that English splits between "tidy" and "organize."

examples.hanzi: 请整理一下你的书桌。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhěnglǐ yíxià nǐ de shūzhuō.
examples.english: Please tidy up your desk.

examples.hanzi: 我正在整理这次旅行的照片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài zhěnglǐ zhè cì lǚxíng de zhàopiàn.
examples.english: I'm sorting through the photos from this trip.

components.note: 斗 (dipper) — a measuring dipper with a handle; as a radical it marks measuring: 料, 科, 斜. Also read dǒu (a measure) or dòu (to fight).

example.hanzi: 我们晚上一起斗地主吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang yìqǐ dòu dìzhǔ ba.
example.english: Let's play Dou Dizhu together tonight.
example.fact: 斗 is read dòu for fighting and competing, from the old 鬥: 斗争 (struggle), 战斗 (battle), 斗地主 (a popular card game, 'fight the landlord'). Read dǒu, it is a ladle or measure, as in 北斗 (the Big Dipper).

examples.hanzi: 两只公鸡在院子里斗起来了。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng zhī gōngjī zài yuànzi li dòu qǐlái le.
examples.english: Two roosters started fighting in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 要努力奋斗才能成功。
examples.pinyin: Yào nǔlì fèndòu cái néng chénggōng.
examples.english: You have to strive hard to succeed.

components.note: 木 (tree) — three trees make a dense forest; 林 is two trees, 森 sēn adds more.
木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.

example.hanzi: 这座森林里有很多野生动物。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò sēnlín lǐ yǒu hěn duō yěshēng dòngwù.
example.english: There are many wild animals in this forest.
example.fact: 森林 stacks two tree-pile pictographs: 木 ("tree") tripled into 森 ("dense forest") and 木 doubled into 林 ("grove, cluster of trees") — a visually literal compound where more repeated tree-strokes really do signal denser woodland, one of the clearest surviving pictographic logics in modern vocabulary.

examples.hanzi: 我们周末去森林里露营。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù sēnlín lǐ lùyíng.
examples.english: We are going camping in the forest this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 森林对保护环境非常重要。
examples.pinyin: Sēnlín duì bǎohù huánjìng fēicháng zhòngyào.
examples.english: Forests are very important for protecting the environment.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.
尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.

example.hanzi: 联邦调查局正在调查这起案件。
example.pinyin: Liánbāng Diàochájú zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ ànjiàn.
example.english: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating this case.
example.fact: 调查局 simply appends 局 ("bureau, office" — the same 局 in 邮局 "post office" and 警察局 "police station") onto 调查 ("to investigate"), giving a transparent "investigation bureau." It's most familiar as the last three characters of 联邦调查局, the standard Chinese name for the American FBI.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是联邦调查局探员的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì Liánbāng Diàochájú tànyuán de gùshi.
examples.english: This movie is about the story of an agent of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

examples.hanzi: 他在调查局工作了二十年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài diàochájú gōngzuò le èrshí nián.
examples.english: He has worked at the bureau of investigation for twenty years.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.
辶 (movement) — marks walking, roads and motion, as in 过 pass, 进 enter, 追 chase; 迫 is to press or drive someone on.
白 (bái) is a loose hint for pò; 拍 pāi and 泊 bó share the same part.

example.hanzi: 别强迫孩子学他们不喜欢的东西。
example.pinyin: Bié qiǎngpò háizi xué tāmen bù xǐhuan de dōngxi.
example.english: Don't force children to learn things they don't like.
example.fact: 强迫 combines 强 ("strong, forceful") with 迫 ("to press, to pressure," as in 迫切 "urgent") — both halves already lean toward coercion on their own. The word commonly appears in the passive construction 被强迫 ("to be forced to").

examples.hanzi: 没有人可以强迫你做不想做的事。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén kěyǐ qiǎngpò nǐ zuò bù xiǎng zuò de shì.
examples.english: Nobody can force you to do things you don't want to do.

examples.hanzi: 他是被强迫签字的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì bèi qiǎngpò qiānzì de.
examples.english: He was forced to sign.

components.note: 卜 (divination) — cracks read on heated bones; 口 below is asking. 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 这张桌子占了很多地方。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi zhàn le hěn duō dìfang.
example.english: This table takes up a lot of space.
example.fact: 占 is zhàn for occupying and for proportions: 占线 (line busy), 占座 (reserve a seat), 占 20% (account for). Read zhān, it means to divine, as in 占卜 (fortune-telling).

examples.hanzi: 他们占了前面的座位。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhàn le qiánmiàn de zuòwèi.
examples.english: They took the seats at the front.

examples.hanzi: 女生占全班的一半。
examples.pinyin: Nǚshēng zhàn quán bān de yíbàn.
examples.english: Girls make up half of the class.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 他们的爱情注定要失败。
example.pinyin: Tāmen de àiqíng zhùdìng yào shībài.
example.english: Their love was destined to fail.
example.fact: 注定 leans on 定 ("fixed, settled") plus 注 (roughly "to inscribe, to note down," as in an official record) — together suggesting fate has already been written down and fixed. The word itself is neutral about good or bad outcomes; only context makes it sound like "doomed" rather than simply "destined."

examples.hanzi: 这件事注定会发生。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì zhùdìng huì fāshēng.
examples.english: This was bound to happen.

examples.hanzi: 他们注定要成为好朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhùdìng yào chéngwéi hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: They are destined to become good friends.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun radical — dark is the lack of daylight; compare 明 bright, 晚 evening.
音 (yīn) — loose sound hint — 暗 is àn; 音 also sounds out 谙 ān.
示 (show) — an altar, a table for offerings; as the radical 礻 it marks rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福, 社, 祝.

example.hanzi: 她的话暗示了她并不高兴。
example.pinyin: Tā de huà ànshì le tā bìng bù gāoxìng.
example.english: Her words hinted that she wasn't happy at all.
example.fact: 暗示 literally means "dark/hidden (暗) indication (示)." Its opposite, 明示 ("to state explicitly"), swaps in 明 ("bright, clear") for 暗 — the same 示 root flips meaning entirely depending on which "light" character precedes it.

examples.hanzi: 他没有直接说，只是暗示我该走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu zhíjiē shuō, zhǐshì ànshì wǒ gāi zǒu le.
examples.english: He didn't say it directly, but hinted that I should go.

examples.hanzi: 老师给了我们一个小暗示。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěi le wǒmen yí ge xiǎo ànshì.
examples.english: The teacher gave us a little hint.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脚 foot, 腿 leg, 脑 brain; 臂 is the arm (手臂).
辟 (pì) hints at the sound; 臂 bì is close to 避 bì and 壁 bì, which share it.

example.hanzi: 他伸出手臂拥抱了朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā shēnchū shǒubì yōngbào le péngyou.
example.english: He stretched out his arm to hug his friend.
example.fact: 手臂 pairs 手 ("hand") with 臂 ("arm") into one word for the whole limb, and it extends figuratively to mean a trusted assistant or "right-hand" helper — the same body-part metaphor English makes with the phrase "right-hand man."

examples.hanzi: 他的手臂上有一道长长的伤疤。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒubì shang yǒu yí dào chángcháng de shāngbā.
examples.english: There is a long scar on his arm.

examples.hanzi: 他是老板最得力的手臂。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì lǎobǎn zuì délì de shǒubì.
examples.english: He is the boss's most capable right-hand man.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
彳 (step, walk) — 彳 is the left-step radical, as in 行, 径, 德; 往 is going toward.
王 (wáng) — near sound — 往 is wǎng, same syllable with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Dàibiǎotuán míngtiān qiánwǎng Běijīng.
example.english: The delegation will head to Beijing tomorrow.
example.fact: 前往 is a formal, written-register word for "to go to," typical of news reports, itineraries, and official announcements. Everyday spoken Mandarin almost always reaches for the plain verb 去 instead, so hearing 前往 signals a noticeably more formal register.

examples.hanzi: 明天我要前往上海参加会议。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ yào qiánwǎng Shànghǎi cānjiā huìyì.
examples.english: Tomorrow I will head to Shanghai for a meeting.

examples.hanzi: 请乘客前往三号登机口。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng chéngkè qiánwǎng sān hào dēngjīkǒu.
examples.english: Passengers are requested to proceed to gate three.

components.note: 谷 (valley) — suggests an open gap, matching the sense of 'open, clear'; 豁 can also mean to exempt (豁免).
害 (hài) is only a loose sound hint for huò.
⺈ (bent figure) — top part, a person; with 口 and 儿 it forms 免. Origin unclear; Memory aid: a person with a hat slipping out, 'excused'.
儿 (legs) — the bottom part and radical, a walking person, as in 先 first and 兄 older brother.

example.hanzi: 外交官享有法律豁免权。
example.pinyin: Wàijiāoguān xiǎngyǒu fǎlǜ huòmiǎnquán.
example.english: Diplomats enjoy legal immunity.
example.fact: 豁免 is formal legal/administrative vocabulary, most often attached to 权 as 豁免权 ("immunity," e.g. diplomatic immunity). 豁 contributes a sense of "opening up, clearing away" (compare 豁达, "open-minded"), reinforcing 免's core meaning of being excused or exempted from something.

examples.hanzi: 学生可以豁免部分费用。
examples.pinyin: Xuésheng kěyǐ huòmiǎn bùfen fèiyòng.
examples.english: Students can be exempted from part of the fees.

examples.hanzi: 这笔钱可以豁免税款。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ qián kěyǐ huòmiǎn shuì kuǎn.
examples.english: This money can be exempted from tax.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 法官询问了案件的当事人。
example.pinyin: Fǎguān xúnwèn le ànjiàn de dāngshìrén.
example.english: The judge questioned the parties involved in the case.
example.fact: 当事人 is standard legal vocabulary for the parties directly involved in a case — literally "the person(s) at (当) the matter (事)." It deliberately stays neutral about role or guilt, unlike more specific legal terms such as 被告 ("defendant") or 原告 ("plaintiff").

examples.hanzi: 当事人不同意这个办法。
examples.pinyin: Dāngshìrén bù tóngyì zhège bànfǎ.
examples.english: The person concerned does not agree to this method.

examples.hanzi: 律师正在和当事人见面。
examples.pinyin: Lǜshī zhèngzài hé dāngshìrén jiànmiàn.
examples.english: The lawyer is meeting with his client.
